passages.provision_quote: C. On conviction of an offense under this article, the judge shall enter an order that requires the person to return to the foreign nation from which the person entered or attempted to enter the United States or the person's nation of origin.
passages.note: Senate engrossed text of the referred measure: illegal entry, return orders, benefits document verification, e-verify false documents and fentanyl sentencing in one act.

rows.reasoning: Gillette's Y on HCR2060 (2024) is a vote on a multi-subject referral that joins return-to-foreign-nation orders with public-benefit document verification, e-verify false-document crimes and fentanyl sentencing, so under the vote ladder it shows direction only. Its return orders reach only people charged with or convicted of entering "directly from a foreign nation at any location other than a lawful port of entry" and the article "may only be enforced prospectively", which does not say that long-settled immigrants should be left "in place" (rung 3) nor that all should be deported "starting with those who have criminal records" (rung 4). No passage ties his vote to one of those rungs' clauses.
